name: Qlane
tagline: An AI product at qlane.ai whose exact job we could not pin down from public material, apparently agent-style workflow automation.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: We are not going to pretend we know this one cold: the public surface is thin, so treat this entry as a shape rather than a teardown. If Qlane is what it looks like, an LLM wrapped in a workflow builder with connectors, then the core loop is genuinely one-shot territory: prompt chains, a run history, a queue, some output formatting. What an agent will not hand you in a session is the boring half, the OAuth dance for every SaaS it touches, retries that survive a rate limit, and a UI that a non-you person can operate. So a weekend gets you a private version that does your two or three real workflows, and nothing that generalizes. Revisit this page once someone verifies what the product actually does and what it costs.
coreLoopDIY: Define reusable prompt pipelines, run them over inputs on demand or on a schedule, and keep every run with its inputs and outputs in a local database.
requirements: Node 20 and a local machine or a cheap VPS
An LLM API key in .env, OpenAI or Anthropic
Any third-party connectors you want wired by hand, one at a time
whatYouLose: Prebuilt connectors and the OAuth plumbing behind them
Hosted scheduling and retries that keep running while your laptop is shut
A UI other people can use without you standing behind them
Error handling for the ugly cases: rate limits, truncated outputs, partial runs
Whatever model routing or prompt tuning the vendor did that you now have to redo by feel
moatNotes: For tools in this shape the moat is almost never the model, it is the hundred connectors and the retry logic nobody enjoys writing.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for AI workflow tools because the value is not the prompt, it is that someone else already handled auth for a dozen SaaS apps, keeps the jobs running when your machine is asleep, and eats the support burden when a model changes behavior overnight. A personal build skips all of that by only ever needing to work for one user with one set of habits. That trade is fine until you want a teammate to touch it.
notes: Listed with low confidence: the pricing and feature set here need a human pass before anyone quotes this page.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI workflow runner. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router and TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- LLM calls through the OpenAI Node SDK, key read from process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY
- Everything runs with: npm install, npm run dev

Data model:
- pipeline: id, name, description, created_at
- step: id, pipeline_id, order_index, name, prompt_template, model, temperature
- run: id, pipeline_id, input_text, status (queued, running, done, failed), started_at, finished_at
- step_result: id, run_id, step_id, rendered_prompt, output_text, tokens_in, tokens_out, error

Behavior:
- A pipeline is an ordered list of steps. Each step's prompt_template may reference {{input}} and {{previous}}. Render, call the model, store the output, feed it to the next step.
- Runs execute in an in-process queue, one at a time, with three retries on 429 or 5xx using exponential backoff. Persist status transitions so a crash leaves a readable record.
- Optional cron-style schedule per pipeline, stored as a cron string, executed by a single node-cron instance in a server-only module. Skip a scheduled run if the previous one is still running.

UI, four pages:
- /pipelines: list, create, delete
- /pipelines/[id]: edit steps, drag to reorder, run now with a text input box
- /runs: reverse-chronological list with status badges
- /runs/[id]: every step with its rendered prompt and raw output, plus a copy button and a JSON export

In scope: local auth-free single user, streaming the current step's output to the run page, markdown rendering of outputs.
Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, third-party SaaS connectors, OAuth, billing, multi-tenancy, a public API.

Deliver a README with setup, an .env.example containing OPENAI_API_KEY, and two seeded example pipelines so the first run works immediately after install.
